q: Did games with smaller crowds coincide with smaller national TV audiences in 2025 and 2026?
title: MLB attendance and national TV audiences, 2025 to 2026
cited: Yes, games with smaller crowds tended to have smaller national TV audiences, but a crowd that was small for its own park did not clearly mean a smaller audience (table: crowd_tv_headline). Comparing games on the same network, the two moved together (correlation 0.34 in 2025, n = 82, range 0.14 to 0.52; 0.47 in 2026, n = 83, range 0.29 to 0.62) (table: crowd_tv_headline). After comparing each game with its own park's usual crowd, the link mostly disappears (0.16 in 2025, range -0.05 to 0.37; 0.14 in 2026, range -0.08 to 0.34; both ranges include zero) (table: crowd_tv_headline). Across team-seasons, teams with higher average home attendance also tended to have larger average national TV audiences (correlation 0.51, n = 56, range 0.29 to 0.68) (table: team_crowd_tv). This is consistent with team-level factors such as popularity and market size, but the data does not show that one causes the other.
report:
Yes, games with smaller crowds tended to have smaller national TV audiences, but a crowd that was small for its own park did not clearly mean a smaller audience[1]. Comparing games on the same network, the two moved together (correlation 0.34 in 2025, n = 82, range 0.14 to 0.52; 0.47 in 2026, n = 83, range 0.29 to 0.62)[1]. After comparing each game with its own park's usual crowd, the link mostly disappears (0.16 in 2025, range -0.05 to 0.37; 0.14 in 2026, range -0.08 to 0.34; both ranges include zero)[1]. Across team-seasons, teams with higher average home attendance also tended to have larger average national TV audiences (correlation 0.51, n = 56, range 0.29 to 0.68)[2]. This is consistent with team-level factors such as popularity and market size, but the data does not show that one causes the other[2].

*Viewership figures are publicly reported and may differ from official Nielsen data. They are the national TV audience, excluding streaming add-ons. Nielsen changed its method on September 1, 2025, so 2025 and 2026 figures are not like-for-like.*

q: Did the Red Sox or the Yankees have better season opener attendance in 2024?
title: Red Sox vs Yankees season opener attendance, 2024
cited: The New York Yankees drew 11,719 fans more than the Boston Red Sox for their 2024 home opener, with the Yankees drawing 47,812 fans to the Red Sox' 36,093 (table: games; query: Q4). The Yankees drew 102.7% of listed capacity at Yankee Stadium, while the Red Sox drew 95.6% of capacity at Fenway Park, representing a gap of 7.1 percentage points (table: games; query: Q4).

q: Which five teams drew the highest average attendance in 2025?
title: Top five teams MLB attendance, 2025
cited: The Los Angeles Dodgers topped the league in 2025 with 49,537 fans per game, leading a top five that also included the Padres, Yankees, Phillies, and Mets (table: team_season_model). The Dodgers drew 88.5% of capacity (table: games_clean), which was 7,102 more fans than the second-place San Diego Padres' average of 42,435 fans (table: team_season_model; query: Q3, Q4). The Padres drew 106.3% of listed capacity (table: games_clean; query: Q3). The New York Yankees were third, averaging 42,408 fans and drawing 91.1% of capacity (table: team_season_model; table: games_clean), just 27 fans behind the Padres (table: team_season_model; query: Q3). The Philadelphia Phillies followed in fourth with 41,672 fans per game and 95.5% of capacity (table: team_season_model; table: games_clean), which was 736 fewer fans than the Yankees (table: team_season_model; query: Q3, Q4). The New York Mets rounded out the top five, averaging 39,316 fans and drawing 94.9% of capacity (table: team_season_model; table: games_clean), representing 2,356 fewer fans than the Phillies (table: team_season_model; query: Q3, Q4).
report: The Los Angeles Dodgers topped the league in 2025 with 49,537 fans per game, leading a top five that also included the Padres, Yankees, Phillies, and Mets[1]. The Dodgers drew 88.5% of capacity, which was 7,102 more fans than the second-place San Diego Padres' average of 42,435 fans[2][1]. The Padres drew 106.3% of listed capacity[2]. The New York Yankees were third, averaging 42,408 fans and drawing 91.1% of capacity, just 27 fans behind the Padres[1][2]. The Philadelphia Phillies followed in fourth with 41,672 fans per game and 95.5% of capacity, which was 736 fewer fans than the Yankees[1][2]. The New York Mets rounded out the top five, averaging 39,316 fans and drawing 94.9% of capacity, representing 2,356 fewer fans than the Phillies[1][2].

q: Rank the networks by average national TV audience in 2026.
title: MLB national TV network audiences, 2026
cited: Fox led all national networks in average TV audience in 2026, topping a list of seven networks. Netflix averaged 2,314,000 viewers across 2 games with known audiences in 2026 (table: network_audience). This put Netflix 29,875 viewers behind Fox (table: network_audience). NBC averaged 2,312,762 viewers across 21 games with known audiences in 2026 (table: network_audience), trailing Netflix by 1,238 viewers (table: network_audience). ABC averaged 1,794,333 viewers across 3 games with known audiences in 2026 (table: network_audience). This was 518,429 viewers fewer than NBC (table: network_audience). ESPN averaged 1,126,208 viewers across 24 games with known audiences in 2026, out of 27 games (table: network_audience), falling 668,125 viewers behind ABC (table: network_audience). TBS averaged 614,900 viewers across 10 games with known audiences in 2026, out of 25 games (table: network_audience). This was 511,308 viewers below ESPN (table: network_audience). FS1 averaged 385,905 viewers across 21 games with known audiences in 2026, out of 39 games (table: network_audience), trailing TBS by 228,995 viewers (table: network_audience).
